title: Verifier‑Grounded Intent→Config Evaluation (paired_success_rate_difference; shared_initial_candidate): A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: Confirmatory estimand (explicit): paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory protocol (shared_initial_candidate per pair) both conditions passed the verifier on all tasks (baseline 120/120; guarded 120/120). Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We publish the complete execution and scoring artifacts (see execution/execution_manifest.json and representative files cited below), diagnose—using archived traces—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate paired contingency, and provide artifact‑grounded, runnable protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed sampling, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question of independent generative reliability. The immutable initial master prompt is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Motivation and scope. Translating operator intent into device configuration is an operationally critical NetOps activity: incorrect commands can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe transient states during multi‑step changes. Deterministic validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) provide auditable, pre‑deployment oracles for generated configurations [Batfish lineage; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Modern LLM pipelines can generate fluent device configuration, but their deployment requires quantified reliability under operational constraints. This study deliberately addresses the evaluation methodology: what exactly does a preregistered paired verifier‑grounded test measure if the same generator candidate is reused across conditions? We preregistered an explicit estimand and a frozen pipeline (CAND‑2026‑001) and executed it end‑to‑end with exhaustive artifact publication to permit byte‑for‑byte reproduction.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation and generate–validate–repair. Prior work couples generative systems with deterministic validators to obtain operational correctness (generate–validate–repair architectures). Empirical studies differ along three axes that materially change interpretability: (A) sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition or multi‑seed sampling), (B) repair budget and loop semantics, and (C) validator scope (syntactic vs. semantic/verifier ensembles). Iterative repair literature shows diminishing returns after a few repair iterations in many domains (see W7167748939 and related entries in the evidence bundle). Our contribution is not a new verifier or a new LLM; it is a preregistered, artifact‑anchored diagnosis of how choice (A) interacts with deterministic validators to produce (or collapse) confirmatory contrasts, together with reproducible rerun specifications.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The full preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) specified: paired design, N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (single canonical candidate per pair), model = gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0), and a fixed analysis script paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap 10,000, seed = 1729). All artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints are published in execution/execution_manifest.json. Task generation and templates. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups) and difficulty metadata. Representative task artifacts and canonical candidate files are archived (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., task-000002-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 ae967f70..., task-000003-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 f7f4db24...). Scoring and validator traces. The validator enforces intent constraints, transient safety policies, and final_state invariants; it emits detailed JSON traces at execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Primary confirmatory analysis. The preregistered estimator is the mean over tasks of (guarded_i − baseline_i) where guarded/baseline are binary verifier passes. In the shared_initial_candidate protocol the same canonical candidate file (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) was used for both conditions in every pair (see execution/provider_calls/* for provider traces). Mapping requested by reviewers (operational question vs. preregistered estimand vs. causal mechanism). To satisfy the reviewer requirement we include the concise mapping below (artifact‑anchored):

- Operational question practitioners typically need: independent per‑condition generative reliability — "If I sample the LLM independently at deployment, what is the probability a generated candidate will pass the validator?" (requires independent_per_condition or multi‑seed sampling; not estimated by the current confirmatory run). 
- Preregistered estimand actually tested here: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with shared_initial_candidate semantics (explicit in preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...). This measures whether a deterministic validator treats identical inputs differently across scoring conditions. Evidence: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c...) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 9c77c96f...).
- Causal reason the confirmatory contingency collapsed: identical canonical candidates per pair + deterministic validator ⇒ identical pass/fail outputs. Supporting artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c...).

Runnable modifications (artifact‑grounded). The archived pipeline permits immediate deterministic reruns to estimate independent reliability without changing templates: (1) independent_per_condition rerun: generate distinct seed per condition per task (e.g., baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1) and rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (2) multi‑seed design: sample K ≥ 3 seeds per condition per task; (3) validator diversification: run additional independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All rerun steps use the same archived task generator and validator binaries (execution/*).
sections.results: Execution and exact confirmatory counts (artifact‑grounded). Execution completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 120 (shared initial generation per pair). The per‑condition aggregated confirmatory counts are archived (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f...): baseline_successes = 120/120; guarded_successes = 120/120. The paired contingency is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Confirmatory inference (preregistered analysis). Primary estimator = mean(guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] from 10,000 resamples (bootstrap seed = 1729 as preregistered). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All analysis artifacts and plots are archived (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...). Representative validator traces. Stored per episode; a representative excerpt is at execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...), which shows parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4 and validation_after.valid = true for that canonical candidate. These traces demonstrate deterministic parsing, transient policy enforcement, and final_state verification for each scored candidate.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The confirmatory statistics are correct for the preregistered estimand: they test whether a deterministic validator treats identical artifacts differently under two scoring conditions. They do not estimate independent generative reliability (the operational probability that independently sampled LLM candidates pass the validator). The artifact record makes the causal mechanism transparent: identical shared_initial_candidate files (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) were reused for both conditions per pair and the deterministic validator returned identical outcomes (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Practical implication: researchers and operators must match sampling semantics to their deployment question—shared candidate protocols test validator determinism and scoring reproducibility; independent sampling estimates the model’s stochastic reliability under deployment. Reproducible corrective reruns. Because every element (task generator, provider call traces, canonical candidates, validator traces, and SHA‑256 manifest) is archived, the community can deterministically rerun the pipeline under independent_per_condition or multi‑seed semantics to obtain informative operational estimates without redefining tasks. Limitations and validity threats (artifact‑recorded): internal validity (shared_initial design removed generation variance), construct validity (template‑tight tasks may overstate success vs. open intents), external validity (single model gpt‑5‑mini and single validator), and contamination uncertainty (string‑overlap heuristics preregistered but imperfect). All limitations are documented and supported by the archived artifacts (analysis/contamination_summary.csv and execution/* traces).
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released exhaustive artifacts sufficient for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate protocol both baseline and guarded conditions passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120), producing a degenerate paired contingency (paired difference = 0.00). The artifact record explains this result unambiguously: identical canonical candidates per pair + deterministic validator ⇒ identical scores. To answer the independent generative reliability question practitioners typically need, the published bundle supports immediate deterministic reruns using independent_per_condition or multi‑seed designs and validator diversification. We provide these runnable, artifact‑grounded recommendations so reproducible follow‑ups can quantify the operational reliability of LLM‑generated network configurations.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
